name: update-integrity-audit
title: Update integrity audit
description: Integrity audit of a P6 schedule update against the previous update: open ends tied to the finish, constraints removed to clear negative float, must finish date moved, actual dates rewritten, durations cut, critical links removed, link types, lags, options and calendars changed, activities deleted, data date, with the questions to raise with the contractor (read only). Use when the user asks to review or audit a submitted update, or what changed in it that needs explaining.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID of the update to review

args.name: previous
args.description: Project ID of the previous update (or a baseline saved from it)

template:
Update integrity audit of project {project} against the previous update {previous}: the changes reviewers question (open ends tied to the finish, constraints removed to clear negative float, must finish date moved, actual dates rewritten, durations cut, critical links removed, link types, lags, options and calendars changed, activities deleted, data date), each with sample rows and a question to raise with the contractor. Read only: nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. ui = p6_update_integrity(project="{project}", other="{previous}", sample_size=10): every flag: count, up to 10 rows.
2. cmp = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", other="{previous}", section="activities", limit=1): both data dates again (cross-check).

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- A flag is a question to raise, not proof of manipulation: copy the caveat of the result, and never call a
  change manipulation, fraud or an error. A change can be a correct revision.
- The questions are the fixed sentences of report.md, one per flag raised: add no other accusation or advice.
- The full list of one flag: p6_update_integrity with flag=<the flag> pages every row (only when the user asks).

# Update integrity audit of {project} against {previous}

Data date of the previous update {dd_before}, of this update {data_date} ({dd_delta} calendar days later). Last schedule run (F9) of this update {last_f9}. Read only: nothing was written to the database.

{caveat}

[if: stale]
Warning: this update was changed after its last F9. Its dates and float are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

## Flags

{raised} of the 11 flags have a count. Each table below shows at most 10 rows of its flag.

[table: summary]

[if: n_open_end]
### Open ends tied to the finish or start ({n_open_end})

[table: t_open_end]

[end if]
[if: n_neg]
### Negative float cleared by a constraint or the must finish date ({n_neg})

[table: t_neg]

[end if]
[if: n_must]
### Must finish by date moved

Previous update {must_before}, this update {must_after}: moved by {must_wd} working days of the project calendar.

[end if]
[if: n_act]
### Actual dates changed ({n_act})

[table: t_act]

[end if]
[if: n_cut]
### Durations cut ({n_cut}, of which critical before: {n_cut_crit})

[table: t_cut]

[end if]
[if: n_links]
### Links removed on critical or near critical work ({n_links})

[table: t_links]

[end if]
[if: n_rel]
### Link types or lags changed ({n_rel})

[table: t_rel]

[end if]
[if: n_opt]
### Schedule options changed ({n_opt})

[table: t_opt]

[end if]
[if: n_cal]
### Calendars changed ({n_cal})

[table: t_cal]

[end if]
[if: n_del]
### Activities deleted while in progress or critical ({n_del})

[table: t_del]

[end if]
[if: n_dd]
### Data date

The data date did not move forward: previous update {dd_before}, this update {data_date}.
[end if]

## Questions to raise with the contractor

[if not: raised]
No flag was raised: there is no question to raise from this comparison.
[end if]
[if: n_open_end]
- Open ends: why were these activities tied straight to the project finish (or start)? Which work do they really drive, or follow?
[end if]
[if: n_neg]
- Negative float: why were these constraints removed or changed, or the must finish date moved, when this cleared negative float? Which recovery of the work supports the new float?
[end if]
[if: n_must]
- Must finish date: was the new must finish by date agreed, by an approved extension of time or change order? Please give its reference.
[end if]
[if: n_act]
- Actual dates: why were actual dates reported in the previous update changed? Please provide the site records that support the new dates.
[end if]
[if: n_cut]
- Durations: what supports the shorter durations (more resources, another method, less scope)? For the critical ones, how will they be achieved?
[end if]
[if: n_links]
- Removed links: why were these links to critical or near critical work removed? Is the logic they stood for no longer valid?
[end if]
[if: n_rel]
- Link types and lags: why were these relationship types or lags changed? Do the new ones match how the work will be done?
[end if]
[if: n_opt]
- Schedule options: why were these scheduling options changed? They change how every date and float is calculated.
[end if]
[if: n_cal]
- Calendars: why were these calendars or calendar assignments changed? Are the new working times and holidays agreed?
[end if]
[if: n_del]
- Deleted activities: why were activities that were in progress or critical deleted? Was their scope completed, moved or removed?
[end if]
[if: n_dd]
- Data date: why did the data date not move forward since the previous update?
[end if]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says a project is not found: "Project <project or previous> was not found: check the Project ID
  (p6_list_projects)."
- p6_update_integrity says other must be another project: "Give the Project ID of the previous update, not the
  update itself."

## Warnings (fixed wording in report.md)

- The caveat of ui is always copied, first after the data dates: a flag is a question, not proof.
- schedule_state.stale is true: keep the warning.
- summary.data_date is 1: keep the data date section and its question.

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. ui.data_date.after = ui.schedule_state.data_date = cmp.projects.last_recalc_date.project (data date of the
   update).
2. ui.data_date.before = cmp.projects.last_recalc_date.other (data date of the previous update).

If a group differs, the database changed between the calls: run the two calls again once. If it still
differs, say which group differs and do not publish the figures it concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The summary table lists the 11 flags in the order returned, with their counts. A flag table and its
  question appear only when its count is not 0; each table shows the sample rows of its flag (at most 10)
  in the order returned. When a count is larger than its table, say nothing more: the count is the figure.
- Activities are written "Activity ID - name"; a calendar is written by its name alone.
- The questions are the fixed sentences of report.md, one per flag raised, worded as questions: never call a
  change manipulation, fraud or an error.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Update integrity audit

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. ui = p6_update_integrity(project="{project}", other="{previous}", sample_size=10): every flag: count, up to 10 rows.
2. cmp = p6_compare_projects(project="{project}", other="{previous}", section="activities", limit=1): both data dates again (cross-check).

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID of the update to review, as given
- {previous}: Project ID of the previous update (or a baseline saved from it), as given

## Units

- wd proj: working days of the project calendar
- cd: calendar days
- d: days of each activity's calendar (hours / hours per day)
- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |

| data_date | ui.schedule_state.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date |
| last_f9 | ui.schedule_state.last_schedule_date |  | datetime | n/a | last F9 of the update |
| stale | ui.schedule_state.stale |  | flag | n/a | changed by this server after the last F9 |
| dd_before | ui.data_date.before |  | date | n/a | previous data date |
| dd_delta | ui.data_date.delta_cd | cd | n1 | n/a | data date moved by |
| raised | ui.raised_count | count | int | n/a | flags with a count |
| n_open_end | ui.summary.open_end_to_finish | count | int | n/a | flag count |
| n_neg | ui.summary.negative_float_cleared_by_constraint | count | int | n/a | flag count |
| n_must | ui.summary.must_finish_moved | count | int | n/a | flag count |
| n_act | ui.summary.actuals_changed | count | int | n/a | flag count |
| n_cut | ui.summary.duration_cut | count | int | n/a | flag count |
| n_cut_crit | ui.flags.duration_cut.critical | count | int | n/a | critical before |
| n_links | ui.summary.links_removed_on_critical | count | int | n/a | flag count |
| n_rel | ui.summary.rel_type_or_lag_changed | count | int | n/a | flag count |
| n_opt | ui.summary.schedule_options_changed | count | int | n/a | flag count |
| n_cal | ui.summary.calendars_changed | count | int | n/a | flag count |
| n_del | ui.summary.deleted_in_progress_or_critical | count | int | n/a | flag count |

| must_before | ui.must_finish.before |  | datetime | none | previous must finish |
| must_after | ui.must_finish.after |  | datetime | none | must finish now |
| must_wd | ui.must_finish.delta_wd | wd proj | n1 | n/a | must finish moved by |
| caveat | ui.caveat |  | text | n/a | what a flag is and is not |

## Questions to raise with the contractor

- Open ends: why were these activities tied straight to the project finish (or start)? Which work do they really drive, or follow?
- Negative float: why were these constraints removed or changed, or the must finish date moved, when this cleared negative float? Which recovery of the work supports the new float?
- Must finish date: was the new must finish by date agreed, by an approved extension of time or change order? Please give its reference.
- Actual dates: why were actual dates reported in the previous update changed? Please provide the site records that support the new dates.
- Durations: what supports the shorter durations (more resources, another method, less scope)? For the critical ones, how will they be achieved?
- Removed links: why were these links to critical or near critical work removed? Is the logic they stood for no longer valid?
- Link types and lags: why were these relationship types or lags changed? Do the new ones match how the work will be done?
- Schedule options: why were these scheduling options changed? They change how every date and float is calculated.
- Calendars: why were these calendars or calendar assignments changed? Are the new working times and holidays agreed?
- Deleted activities: why were activities that were in progress or critical deleted? Was their scope completed, moved or removed?
